explanation: The discovery trace shows frame_len=3 when the oracle expects 1 at cycle 5. The stimulus has a single valid/ready/tlast=1 cycle with tkeep=1 (one enabled byte). The original RTL executes the tlast branch (sets valid, clears frame_reg) and then also executes the KEEP_ENABLE block, adding the enabled-byte count for that last word a second time. The fix is to prevent the KEEP_ENABLE block from running on the tlast cycle. patch_6ae7345a2b8e does this precisely by adding !monitor_axis_tlast to the KEEP_ENABLE condition at line 95. Other candidates either miss the root cause, are too broad (breaking single-word frames), or invert the required logic.

ranking.mechanism: The KEEP_ENABLE block at line 95 runs on every valid/ready cycle, including the final (tlast=1) cycle. On that cycle the original code also executes the tlast branch (line 84) which sets frame_len_valid_next=1 and frame_next=0, but then the KEEP_ENABLE block still adds the enabled-byte count for the last word. This double-counts the final word, producing frame_len=3 instead of 1 in the discovery trace. Guarding the KEEP_ENABLE block with !monitor_axis_tlast ensures the enabled-byte count is added only for non-last words, matching the spec to count bytes on valid/ready transfers and report on the completed frame.

The outer guard at line 81 currently executes its body on every valid/ready cycle. Adding !monitor_axis_tlast restricts the frame_len update logic to non-last cycles, so the final word does not increment frame_len_next at all (the tlast branch only emits frame_len_valid). This also prevents the double-count but is coarser: it disables the new-frame reset (!frame_reg branch) on a single-word frame where tlast arrives with frame_reg=0, which could break consecutive single-word frames. patch_6ae7345a2b8e is more surgical.

Adding !frame_reg to the tlast condition makes the frame_len_valid pulse conditional on already being inside a frame. This does not address the extra addition performed by the KEEP_ENABLE block on the last cycle, so the frame_len mismatch remains. It also risks suppressing the valid pulse for legitimate single-word frames (frame_reg=0 when tlast arrives).

Guarding the KEEP_ENABLE block with !frame_reg would allow the enabled-byte count only when a frame is already open. On the first word of a frame (frame_reg=0) the count would be skipped, causing an off-by-one on multi-word frames and breaking single-word frames. The failure is on the last word, not the first.
Requiring monitor_axis_tlast on the outer guard inverts the logic: frame_len would only update on the last cycle, breaking all multi-word frames. Does not match the observed single mismatch.

Adding !frame_reg inside the popcount loop makes the bit-count conditional on frame_reg, but the loop still runs on the last cycle. The root cause is the loop executing on the tlast cycle at all; this patch does not stop that.

Clears frame_len_next after frame_len_valid_reg is asserted, which is a post-report reset. The discovery mismatch is the value reported (3 vs 1), not a stale value afterward. This does not prevent the over-count during the final cycle.
Guarding KEEP_ENABLE with monitor_axis_tlast would enable the popcount only on the last cycle — the exact opposite of what is needed — and would still over-count that cycle.
